newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles sharply higher with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles sharply higher with cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled sharply higher Friday with strong cash market prices tied to emerging air-conditioning demand in the Southwest and tight hydropower supply in the Northwest.
Spot power prices at the California-Oregon Border (COB) rose 50 cents to $1 to $19.00-$20.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), while those at Palo Verde (PV) jumped $1-2 to $20.00-21.50.
COB futures took the helm in pushing the complex higher after PV futures led yesterday's rally in record volume.
May COB futures finished up 74 cents at $14.03 after posting a session high at $14.20. June COB ended up 57 cents at $13.45. Other COB months settled flat to up 42 cents.
May PV futures finished up 55 cents at $17.50, trimming an 80 cent gain. June PV ended up 37 cents at $18.57. Other active PV contracts settled five to 10 cents higher.
Hydroelectric output in Northwest has been running relatively low in recent weeks due to a slower-than-normal snowmelt and spillage on the Snake and Columbia Rivers.
Spot power availability in the West has also been reduced by a number of planned and unplanned plant outages.
The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 on the central California coast, set to shut Saturday for a 36-day refueling and maintenance outage, the sources said.
The 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit remained shut for refueling and maintenance, with an expected restart date in late June.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state was also shut for refueling, and was expected to resume power output in early July.
In addition, nearly 6,000 MW of thermal generating capacity was off-line in the West for planned and unplanned maintenance, as well as hydropower displacement sales.
Market sources said the complex will likely continue its recent uptrend next week before May contracts' expiration on Thursday.
